note: Ground truth for the blind set: which requests are the same underlying need. Written at the same time as personas.json and before any run, so the clustering is scored against a fixed answer rather than against whatever it happened to produce. A need with two or more DIFFERENT owners is one a correct system should eventually surface; a need held by one owner, however often they ask, must never be.

hard_pairs.why: Both are reading text off an image. A system that merges them would report one need where there are two, and a builder would close the wrong one.
Both are 'look something up about a website'. Different needs entirely; one is availability, the other is registration.
Both extract content from a document. Merging them would hide a real need behind a more common one.
Both are 'summarise a document into the bits that matter'. The closest legitimate pair in the set.

what_this_measures: Whether clustering recovers the needs that were written down before it ran.
Whether it keeps the hard pairs apart, which is where a single threshold fails.
The similarity distribution within a need against the distribution across needs - the gap between them is what a threshold can be set from, and if they overlap there is no correct threshold to find.
Whether the distinct-owner counts come out as labelled, which is the anti-manufacturing rule working.
what_this_does_not_measure: Retrieval recall. Phase 0 measured that on a set written before the corpus existed, and I have since read the corpus - so any recall number from this set would be contaminated and is deliberately not reported.

Whether real people would phrase things this way. These are my guesses at how strangers type, and the whole set shares one author, which is the standing limitation of a simulation and cannot be fixed from inside it.
